description: Buffer overflow gated behind a UART RXNE busy-poll -- the prompt's #1 named hard problem ('bare-metal code often blocks on register polls that will hang a naive emulator'). Both twins require the same MMIO poll-breaking to reach at all; only the bad twin lacks a bound check.

cases.reason: cmd[8] is written with no bound check on the loop index i. Feeding more than 8 bytes before a newline through the emulated UART0->DR overflows cmd. Requires the emulator's MMIO layer to (a) break the RXNE poll loop instead of hanging, and (b) actually vary the injected bytes -- a naive stub returning a constant would either hang forever or never trigger the overflow.
failure_modes_if_wrong: Naive MMIO (always return 0 for SR): uart_getc() spins forever -> wrongly reported as hang/Inconclusive/unreachable.
MMIO that unblocks RXNE but always feeds the same byte or immediately '\n': loop exits after 1 iteration -> bug never triggers, wrongly reported as FP.

cases.reason: Same MMIO poll-loop reachability requirement as bad.elf (this must still be reached, not short-circuited), but the write index is bounds-checked (i < sizeof(cmd)) before every write. No OOB write occurs for any sequence of injected bytes.
